claims.claim: Fréchette states that Élisabeth Vonarburg translated Kay's English name Guinevere by the modern French Geneviève rather than the older Guenièvre.
claims.source: Amélie Fréchette, mémoire de maîtrise, Université Laval, 2013, note 42
claims.quote: a traduit le nom anglais
claims.page: note 42, p. 31

claims.claim: Fréchette judges that this translation choice diminishes the effect the legendary name can produce in the reader's imagination.
claims.source: Amélie Fréchette, mémoire de maîtrise, Université Laval, 2013, note 42
claims.quote: ce choix de traduction diminue à mon avis l’effet
claims.page: note 42, p. 31

claims.claim: Kay writes that the narrator Simon Vance sent him a note about needing to pause at times to control emotion while reading Children of Earth and Sky aloud.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings journal, Children of Earth and Sky (author's post, c. April 2016)
claims.quote: needing to pause at times to control emotion as he read
claims.page: Children of Earth and Sky journal, post announcing the finished audiobook
claims.routeHint: live fetch with browser UA; grep 'Vance'
claims.confidence: medium — Kay paraphrasing Vance's private note, not Vance's own transcribed words

claims.claim: Kay says he often makes adjustments to his text after reading his writing aloud.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings journal, Children of Earth and Sky (author's post on proofing typeset pages)
claims.quote: I often make adjustments after doing that.
claims.page: Children of Earth and Sky journal, post on typesetting and page proofs

claims.claim: Kay says he uses punctuation variably depending on context, speaker and rhythms.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, 2006
claims.quote: I’ll use punctuation varaibly depending on context, speaker, rhythms.
claims.page: Ysabel journal, post on proofreading (Sept./Oct. 2006)

claims.claim: Kay states that The Last Light of the Sun is punctuated differently from the Sarantine Mosaic.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, 2006
claims.quote: LAST LIGHT is punctuated differently than the MOSAIC was.
claims.page: Ysabel journal, post on proofreading (2006)

claims.claim: Kay says that adding a semi-colon or too many technically viable commas to a passage of rapid, stressed speech undermines the effect of the passage.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, 2006
claims.quote: undermines the EFFECT of the passage
claims.page: Ysabel journal, post on the proofreader over-punctuating speech

claims.claim: Kay describes his exchanges with his copy-editor as comma, semi-colon, paragraph break, tense shift and word-choice wars.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings journal, Children of Earth and Sky
claims.quote: comma, semi-colon, paragraph break, tense shift, word-choice wars
claims.page: Children of Earth and Sky journal, post on copy-editing

claims.claim: Kay states that hearing a reading aloud is not the same as reading a book.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Under Heaven tour journal, 2010
claims.quote: Hearing a reading aloud isn’t reading a book.
claims.page: Under Heaven tour journal, post on touring and sharing

claims.claim: Kay says what works when reading alone to yourself is not the same as what works when listening in public.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, November 2006
claims.quote: what works when you are reading alone to yourself is not
claims.page: Ysabel journal, 20 November 2006 post on his first public reading from Ysabel

claims.claim: Kay's site records that Simon Vance read Under Heaven for the audiobook as he had for Tigana and the Fionavar trilogy.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Under Heaven tour journal, 18 February 2010
claims.quote: do the reading, as he did for Tigana and the Fionavar trilogy
claims.page: Under Heaven tour journal, 18 February 2010

claims.claim: Kay states he is not an audio book person.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Under Heaven tour journal, 18 February 2010
claims.quote: I’m not an audio book person
claims.page: Under Heaven tour journal, 18 February 2010

claims.claim: Kay writes that a reader of his work in Russian, Korean or Portuguese is reading someone else's rendering of him.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, October 2006
claims.quote: you are reading someone else’s rendering of me
claims.page: Ysabel journal, October 2006 post on the Giller Prize and translation

claims.claim: Kay states that a translated work is a version and an interpretation of the original author's work rather than that author's own.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, October 2006
claims.quote: It is a version, an interpretation, of that person’s work.
claims.page: Ysabel journal, October 2006 post on translation and the Giller Prize

claims.claim: Kay says he has had readers report that a given book's translation in a given language is terrible.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, Brightweavings Ysabel journal, October 2006
claims.quote: the gift or the burden of the people who carry my work
claims.page: Ysabel journal, October 2006 post on translation
claims.confidence: medium — the quotation supports the surrounding passage on translators rather than the reader reports sentence itself

claims.claim: Vonarburg says that seeing multiple points of view in practice through what Kay does with them, and writing them herself while translating, was different from knowing the theory.
claims.source: Élisabeth Vonarburg, interviewed by Yann Etienne, Diacritik, 19 February 2021
claims.quote: les voir en pratique à travers ce qu’en fait Kay
claims.page: answer to the question on having been a translator

claims.claim: Vonarburg says that translation, for a writer, is still writing.
claims.source: Élisabeth Vonarburg, interviewed by Yann Etienne, Diacritik, 19 February 2021
claims.quote: la traduction, pour une écrivaine, c’est encore de l’écriture
claims.page: answer to the question on having been a translator

claims.claim: Cabon names an illustrated clothing encyclopedia, Sophie George's Le vêtement de A à Z, as particularly useful for his translation of A Brightness Long Ago.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, translator's own page for Comme un diamant dans ma mémoire (L'Atalante, 2023)
claims.quote: particulièrement utile pour cette traduction
claims.page: Références section
claims.routeHint: live fetch of the translator's own site

claims.claim: Cabon says a Chinese mythology dictionary let him solve many puzzles tied to Chinese legends while translating Under Heaven.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, translator's own page for Les Chevaux célestes (L'Atalante, 2014)
claims.quote: m'a permis de résoudre bien des énigmes liées aux légendes chinoises
claims.page: Références section
claims.routeHint: live fetch of the translator's own site

claims.claim: Cabon says he tried to keep Billeter's reflection on the difficulties of translating Chinese poetry in mind throughout his own work on River of Stars.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, translator's own page for Le Fleuve céleste (L'Atalante)
claims.quote: que je me suis efforcé de garder à l'esprit pendant mes propres travaux
claims.page: Références section
claims.routeHint: live fetch of the translator's own site

claims.feature: other: invented world as historical ethic
claims.claim: Cabon writes that one reason Kay sets fact-based plots in invented worlds is his refusal to betray historical figures by presuming their reactions and feelings.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, « Les Chevaux célestes pour "les cancres" », Éditions L'Atalante, 11 July 2014
claims.quote: son refus de trahir les personnages historiques en présumant de leurs réactions
claims.page: opening section

claims.claim: Kattnig asserts that Kay's writing is not an end in itself and serves his story.
claims.source: Alain Kattnig, Éditions L'Atalante blog, 4 July 2014
claims.quote: L’écriture de Guy Gavriel Kay n’est pas une fin et sert son histoire.
claims.page: body of the post

claims.claim: The translator's own pages for Voile vers Sarance and Le Seigneur des empereurs carry the line announcing Kay's Byzantine epic in a new translation.
claims.source: Mikael Cabon, translator's own pages for the Sarantine Mosaic (L'Atalante)
claims.quote: DANS UNE NOUVELLE TRADUCTION
claims.page: back-cover text reproduced on the page
claims.routeHint: live fetch of the translator's own site

claims.claim: Elbakin forum readers record that A Brightness Long Ago exists in two French versions, Vonarburg's Un éclat d'antan for Alire and Cabon's Comme un diamant dans ma mémoire for L'Atalante.
claims.source: Elbakin.net forum thread on Comme un diamant dans ma mémoire (reader posts)
claims.quote: Il avait déjà été traduit par Élisabeth Vonarburg et paru en 2020
claims.page: page 4 of the thread
